page: Vultr voc-g-64c-192gb-960s-amd belongs to the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured to provide dedicated, highly parallel compute capacity paired with local solid-state storage. The instance operates on the x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Hardware allocations include 32 physical cores presenting 64 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core, 32 MB of L3 cache, and 192 GB of total system RAM, establishing a ratio of 3.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via an integrated 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong sustained multi-threaded execution across dense computational suites. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3143.25 alongside a multi-core score of 100556.13, placing it within the upper quartile of evaluated machines. Extended instruction set support includes AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) along with hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. PassMark CPU testing reaches 79514.14 points, backed by strong execution in Clang software compilation at 39811.0 points and ray tracing benchmarks reaching 70617.0 points.

Memory subsystem testing reveals high data throughput, scoring 3067.69 in PassMark memory testing, with uncached 256 MB sequential read throughput of 340.62 GB/sec and write speeds of 163.16 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the server registers 87.2 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 30485.59 points on PassMark database operations, and 47.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 3421.5 tokens per second on compact 135M parameter models, while text generation on 7B models achieves 53.85 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high thread density and low-latency NVMe disk access against a moderate per-core memory footprint. The 3.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes it cost-efficient for core-heavy workloads where larger memory allocations would remain underutilized. The configuration is best aligned with concurrent web application hosting, Redis caching tiers, Clang-based CI/CD compilation pipelines, parallel relational database engines, and CPU-driven vector analytics.

It provides 192 GB of system RAM, offering 3.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates a 960 GB local NVMe SSD without GPU hardware. Benchmark results place the server in the upper quartile for multi-core compute, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 100556.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 79514.14. Memory and storage bandwidth demonstrate strong capabilities, recording 87.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 47.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. While its memory-to-core ratio is moderate, the high core density and bundled NVMe drive make it efficient for multi-threaded build farms, relational databases, in-memory caches, and concurrent application serving.
